entries.title: Cooling system — description and operation
entries.content: The cooling system consists of the radiator, pressure-type filler cap, fan, fan belt, water pump, thermostat, and temperature gage. It is a sealed system operating under pressure when the engine is warmed up. The filler pipe is in the top of the radiator at the right side. There are two drain cocks: one in the radiator outlet at the lower left corner, and one in the right side of the cylinder block at the forward end. The water pump draws coolant from the bottom of the radiator, forces it through the cylinder block, past the thermostat, and back to the radiator, where it is cooled by the fan drawing air through the core.

entries.title: Cooling system capacity
entries.content: Cooling system capacity: 11 quarts (US). Fill to the bottom of the baffle visible through the radiator filler hole — do not overfill.

entries.title: Thermostat operating temperatures
entries.content: Thermostat opens between 140°F and 155°F; fully open at 170°F. Bellows type, located in the water outlet elbow on top of the cylinder head.

entries.title: Radiator cap pressure
entries.content: The pressure-type filler cap maintains up to 4¼ lb pressure, for better engine efficiency and to prevent coolant evaporation. CAUTION: when the engine is warm, release pressure by turning the cap slightly before removal.

entries.title: Fan belt tension (deflection)
entries.content: Adjust the fan belt to about one inch of deflection midway between the fan and generator pulleys. Do NOT adjust the belt extremely tight — this causes excessive wear on water pump and generator bearings. Belt is V-type, 42-degree vee angle.

entries.title: Radiator — fin-and-tube type
entries.content: Fin-and-tube type core with a coolant tank at the top and a sediment tank at the bottom, located at the front of the vehicle. Fitted with a pressure-type filler cap (up to 4¼ lb).

entries.title: Water pump — centrifugal type
entries.content: Centrifugal-impeller type, located in the front end of the cylinder block. Double-row ball bearing integral with the shaft, packed with lubricant at manufacture — NO lubrication attention required. A packless self-sealing gland prevents water leakage and also requires no attention. Driven with the generator and fan by a belt from the engine crankshaft fan pulley.

entries.title: Fan — four-blade, 15 inch
entries.content: Four-blade, 15-inch fan that draws air through the radiator core. Mounted on the front end of the water pump shaft, driven from the crankshaft by the same belt that drives the generator.

entries.title: Temperature gage — Bourdon capillary type
entries.content: Bourdon type with a capillary tube connecting the panel gage to an expansion bulb in the right side of the cylinder head. The entire system is sealed into one assembly — if any difficulty is experienced, the whole assembly must be replaced.

entries.title: Engine overheated from low coolant — do not add cold water immediately
entries.content: If the engine overheats due to lack of coolant, do NOT add cold water immediately. Let the engine cool until the radiator is not boiling, then start the engine and add water slowly — this prevents cracking damage to the cylinder block and head.

entries.title: Cooling system routine maintenance points
entries.content:
1. Keep sufficient coolant in the system: clean water plus the specified rust inhibitor; below 32°F add the proper quantity of antifreeze.
2. Drain, flush, and refill whenever inspection reveals rust or scale; clean seasonally and before/after antifreeze use.
3. Do not overfill — fill to the bottom of the baffle visible through the filler hole.
4. Keep cylinder head, water pump, hose clamps, and connections leakproof; replace deteriorated or leaky hose.
5. Adjust the fan belt and replace as required.
6. Test periodically for air suction and exhaust gas leaking into the system.
Note: when draining, refer to the caution plate on the instrument panel.

entries.title: Draining and refilling the cooling system
entries.content:
Draining:
1. Open the drain cocks at the lower left corner of the radiator and at the right front corner of the cylinder block.
2. Loosen the pressure-type radiator cap to break any vacuum that might prevent proper draining.
3. If the solution is to be saved, catch it in a clean container.
4. If the system is not refilled immediately, attach a tag to the steering wheel warning personnel the system is drained.

Refilling:
1. Close both drain cocks tightly.
2. Use clean water, preferably soft water (low alkali content).
3. Fill through the radiator filler pipe until level reaches the lower edge of the baffle visible through the filler hole.
4. Install the radiator cap, turning clockwise to tighten.
5. Start engine, warm up, check coolant level, and top up if required.

entries.title: Air suction test
entries.content:
Determines if air is entering the coolant (low coolant level, leaky water pump, or loose hose connections):
1. Fill system to the bottom edge of the baffle in the top of the radiator.
2. Replace the pressure cap with a plain cap, tightened airtight.
3. Attach rubber tubing to the lower end of the overflow pipe (connection must be airtight).
4. Run the engine, transmission in neutral, at moderate speed until warmed up.
5. Place the tubing in a glass container of water and, without changing engine speed, watch for bubbles.
6. Continuous bubbles indicate air entering the coolant — find and correct the cause.

entries.title: Exhaust gas leakage test
entries.content:
Determines if exhaust gas is entering the coolant (leaky cylinder block, head, or gasket). NOTE: make this test with the engine COLD.
1. Remove the fan belt.
2. Open the radiator drain cock until coolant is below the cylinder head water outlet.
3. Loosen the three screws holding the outlet to the head, and remove the water outlet.
4. Fill the cylinder head with coolant up to the top of the head.
5. With transmission in neutral, start the engine and "gun" it several times, watching for bubbles in the water.
6. Bubbles indicate leakage. Replace a leaky gasket; report other causes to higher authority.

entries.title: Cleaning and flushing the cooling system
entries.content:
1. Run engine at moderate speed to stir up loose rust.
2. Drain the cooling system.
3. Close drain cocks and fill with the specified cleaning compound; install radiator cap.
4. Operate the engine as directed for the prescribed solution, then stop and completely drain via both drain cocks.
5. To flush: close drain cocks, fill with water, run engine until warm (or run water through), then completely drain.
6. Close drain cocks, refill, and add corrosion inhibitor compound to prevent rust and scale. Renew the inhibitor periodically to stay effective.

entries.title: Radiator removal and installation
entries.content:
Removal:
1. Remove the radiator filler cap.
2. Open the drain cocks on the radiator outlet and the right front corner of the cylinder block; drain the system.
3. Remove the radiator stay rod nut at the front end.
4. Loosen the upper hose clamp at the front end and the hose connection at the water pump.
5. Remove the two radiator hold-down nuts and lift off the radiator; remove drain cock and pads.

Installation:
1. Install drain cock, place pads on bracket, and set radiator in place. NOTE: a light coating of grease in the hose connections eases assembly.
2. Install the stay rod and tighten the lock nut.
3. Tighten upper and lower hose clamps; install hold-down nuts and bond strap.
4. Close both drain cocks, fill the radiator, install the cap, and check for leaks.
5. Start engine, check coolant level when warm, and top up to proper level.

entries.title: Water pump removal and installation
entries.content:
Removal:
1. Open the radiator drain cock and the cylinder block drain cock; remove the filler cap.
2. Pull up on the generator brace handle to loosen the fan belt, and slip off the belt.
3. Loosen the pump hose clamp and remove the hose.
4. Remove the fan blade screws.
5. Remove the screws holding the water pump in the cylinder block, and remove the pump.

Installation:
1. Check the pump-to-block gasket; replace if damaged.
2. Install pump in the cylinder block and tighten the screws.
3. Install fan and screws.
4. Install the fan belt, and pull the generator out until the brace drops into position.
5. Attach the hose connection, fill the radiator, install the cap, and check for leaks. Check coolant level after warm-up.

entries.title: Fan belt removal, installation, and adjustment
entries.content:
Removal:
1. Pull up on the generator brace handle and move the generator toward the engine as far as it will go.
2. Remove the belt from the generator, pump, and crankshaft pulleys, and lift it over the fan blades.

Installation and adjustment:
1. Place the belt over the fan and crankshaft pulleys, then over the generator pulley.
2. Pull the generator out until the brace locks in position.
3. To adjust tension: loosen the generator brace nut and move the generator until the belt has about one inch of deflection midway between the fan and generator pulleys, then tighten the nut.
CAUTION: do not adjust extremely tight — it wears out water pump and generator bearings.

entries.title: Fan removal and installation
entries.content:
Removal:
1. Remove the four screws holding the fan on the fan pulley.
2. Lift the fan out of the shroud.

Installation:
1. Place the fan in position on the fan pulley.
2. Install the four screws and tighten securely.

entries.title: Thermostat removal and installation
entries.content:
Removal:
1. Drain the cooling system via the drain cock at the lower left side of the radiator.
2. Loosen the hose clamp at the cylinder head water outlet elbow; remove three screws and lift off the elbow.
3. Pull out the thermostat retaining ring in the elbow and take out the thermostat.

Installation:
1. Place the thermostat in the water outlet elbow with the BELLOWS DOWN, so coolant reaches the bellows and operates the valve.
2. Install the retaining ring with the flanged edge against the thermostat.
3. Check gasket and cylinder head surface; fit a new gasket if necessary.
4. Insert the outlet elbow in the hose connection, install on the cylinder head with three screws, and tighten the hose connection.
5. Close the drain cock and fill the system (with antifreeze if required). Start engine and check for leaks when warm.

entries.title: Temperature gage removal and installation
entries.content:
Removal:
1. Drain the cooling system via the drain cock under the left side of the radiator.
2. Remove the engine unit (expansion bulb) in the right side of the cylinder head by unscrewing the retaining nut in the reducing bushing.
3. Remove the two nuts holding the retaining bracket on the back of the gage.
4. Remove the grommet around the tube through the dash, and draw out the gage assembly, tube, and engine unit through the hole in the panel.

Installation:
1. Insert the engine unit through the hole in the panel, mounting bracket, and dash.
2. Position the gage, install the mounting bracket and nuts, and tighten.
3. Insert the grommet in the dash; install the engine unit and tighten the retaining nut.
4. Fill the cooling system and check for leaks.
Note: the gage is a sealed one-piece assembly — replace the whole unit if faulty.
